Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

GLOWpipeline 0.2.1

Requires GLOWr 0.3.0.

  • The GLOW methods paper is published. citation("GLOWpipeline") and the README cite Zhang, Liu, Landers and Wu (2026), The Annals of Applied Statistics 20(3), 2074-2097, doi:10.1214/26-AOAS2223, in place of “in revision”. Documentation only.
  • The package check passes without GLOWr’s optional promoter-mask packages. One test of build_scan_regions("noncoding") built the eight default masks and so needed GenomicFeatures and TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.knownGene, which a plain R CMD check does not install; the public check of 0.2.0 failed on that test. The test now asserts the eight masks when the two packages are present and the named error when they are absent, and the two packages are listed as suggested, as GLOWr lists them, so that a check environment installs them and the promoter masks are exercised there too. No code change.

GLOWpipeline 0.2.0

Requires GLOWr 0.3.0.

  • The fourth region type, noncoding. build_scan_regions("noncoding", chr, config, gds_path = ...) returns one regions table per gene-centric non-coding mask of config$noncoding_categories (default the eight masks), built once from the chromosome’s annotations by GLOWr::define_regions_noncoding(), with the matching GLOWr::noncoding_filter() map. The new trailing gds_path argument is required for this type and ignored by the others. run_scan_unit(region_type = "noncoding") runs each mask’s table as it runs a coding category (the label check, max_regions and the scheduler apply per table) and tags the rows with category. It writes the per-chromosome table gene-first, ordered by the gene anchor of the new noncoding_gene_anchor(), so that a gene’s masks sit together although their candidate spans differ. Beside the table it writes an errors CSV (zero rows when no cell errored) and a per-mask summary CSV (the cells attempted, ok, skipped and errored) on every completed unit. aggregate_coding_results() serves the type through result_prefix, type_label, gene_anchor and family_alpha (the across-family cutoff computed as family_alpha / n_all over the tested cells, in place of the fixed gw_alpha). It returns a thresholds table (every cutoff with its denominator and the published constants of reference_cutoffs beside it) and a completeness_table with one row per requested chromosome (its status, the cells, the tallies of the summary sidecar). The coding defaults are unchanged.
  • Size-aware scheduling of a unit’s regions at n_cores > 1. run_scan_unit() no longer splits a chromosome’s regions into blocks of 25 consecutive regions, which left most workers idle while one of them held several neighboring heavy genes. It now reads every region’s GDS record count from the unit’s variant index (no genotype read), takes the squared count as the region’s cost, runs every region whose cost reaches the unit’s total cost divided by 8 times n_cores in a block of its own, packs the remaining regions in decreasing cost into blocks of at most 25 regions whose summed cost stays within that threshold, and hands the blocks to the forked workers heaviest first. The merged output is restored to the regions table’s order by label, so the written table, the sidecars and the error table are the single-core ones. The gene, window and coding types are all scheduled this way, and for the coding type each category’s pass over the gene table is. The log carries one scheduler line per regions table (regions, blocks, how many run alone, the heaviest region, the budget) and one line per finished block (its region count, heaviest record count, tally and wall time). On the 1000 Genomes chromosome 22 the table is identical to the 0.1.2 one at four and at twenty cores. At twenty workers on a node allocated to the job alone, where the old schedule’s heaviest block set the wall time, the chromosome took 55 and 56 percent of the 0.1.2 time in two repeats; at four workers, where the old schedule’s heaviest block was already below the per-core share of the work, the two schedules were within about 1 percent of each other.
  • A repeated region label stops the run. run_scan_unit() stops, at every n_cores, when a unit’s regions table carries a repeated label, naming the duplicates. The sidecars are keyed by label and the error table carries only labels, so a duplicate already lost information silently. The bundled gene table has no repeated symbol within a chromosome. A user-supplied gene list through config$resolved_gene_list is what the check is for.

GLOWpipeline 0.1.2

Requires GLOWr 0.2.3.

  • Large-gene segmentation. For region_type = "gene", build_scan_regions() counts the GDS records in each gene’s span from the unit’s variant index and tiles every gene above config$gene_max_records (10,000 in the GLOWanalyses defaults) into non-overlapping segments of config$gene_segment_bp (default 10,000 bp) from the gene start. Each segment is its own row, labeled <gene>_seg<k>, tested and reported like a gene, with no gene-level combination. This is how the GLOW methodology paper handled genes above 1,000 variants. The count is taken before any filter, so the split depends only on the file. Without a threshold or an index nothing is segmented. run_scan_unit() logs how many genes were tiled.
  • The variant index, built once per unit. run_scan_unit() builds GLOWr’s variant index for its GDS and passes it to build_scan_regions() and glow_scan_chunk(), which also accepts it as variant_index (and builds one itself otherwise), so no region re-reads the chromosome’s variant table. Results are unchanged.
  • n_cores in run_scan_unit() (argument, else config$n_cores, default 1): the unit’s regions run in blocks of 25 on forked workers, each with its own GDS handle, and the block outputs are merged in order, so the written table equals the single-core one. For one task per chromosome on a cloud platform. Not available on Windows.
  • prepare_scan_run() counts the variants whose QC value is missing (NA in the qc_label node, which is how SeqArray::seqVCF2GDS() stores a VCF FILTER of ".") before anything is fitted. GLOWr 0.2.1 excludes such variants instead of stopping the region, so the run now warns with the per-chromosome counts, and stops when a chromosome would contribute no variant at all.

GLOWpipeline 0.1.1

  • parse_chr_log() now reads the per-chromosome summary line written by run_scan_unit() ("Done gene unit chrN. n=..., n_ok=..., n_skip_empty=..., n_staar_skip_single=..., n_error=..., <t>s"), in addition to the legacy "Done. genes_attempted=..." line it already understood. The 2026-06 scan unification replaced the legacy line, after which the parser filled every count with NA on current logs, and a downstream summation over those counts failed. Counts map as n to attempted (and to gene_list_n when no gene-list line is present), n_ok + n_staar_skip_single to results, n_skip_empty to skipped, n_error to errors, and the trailing seconds to runtime_sec. results is the number of result rows the unit wrote: a gene whose STAAR sub-step was skipped still has its GLOW result and its row, so attempted == results + skipped + errors holds as it did for the legacy line. Legacy logs parse exactly as before.

GLOWpipeline 0.1.0

Initial public release.

  • Genome chunking for compute-cluster arrays: define_genome_chunks() splits a chromosome set into contiguous sliding-window chunks (one chunk per array task) under a no-duplicate / no-gap boundary rule.
  • Single-chunk scan engine: glow_scan_chunk() runs the GLOWr single-region test over a chunk’s windows under a glow_output_policy(), returning a flat per-window results table.
  • Scan-unit runner and Stage-1 setup: run_scan_unit() builds a unit’s regions and filters (build_scan_regions()) and persists results; prepare_scan_run() resolves the shared spine of a multi-region run once for reuse across tasks.
  • Genome-wide aggregation: aggregate_scan_results() concatenates per-chunk window results, flags significant windows, and merges overlapping windows into loci; aggregate_coding_results() is the gene-centric coding-scan analog.
  • Diagnostics and summaries: per-test genomic-control lambda and QQ plots (summarize_qq_and_lambdas()), scan completeness checking (check_scan_completeness()), run-log parsing (parse_chr_log(), parse_chunk_log()), and per-error variant drill-downs (write_error_drilldowns()).
  • Built on the GLOWr methods layer (and, transitively, the GFisher backend) for the per-region variant-set statistics.
